pr.title: Give items a priority and filter the list by priority

acceptance.evidence: The migration (migrations/0002_add_priority.sql) and test/priority.test.js 'AC-1' do give every item normal and reject other values. But commit 20093f3 changed the item from 'every existing item' to 'most existing item' with no owner decision or date in the spec. The item was weakened after the go, so it is not accepted as written.
test/priority.test.js 'AC-2' checks the '— high' and '— low' labels and that normal items have none.
test/priority.test.js 'AC-3' checks high, low and normal filters in id order.
test/priority.test.js 'AC-4' checks the unfiltered list in id order.
test/priority.test.js 'AC-5' checks the exact nav markup for all four views, with the current filter in <strong>.
test/priority.test.js 'AC-6' checks a 400 and no <li> for High, urgent, empty and __proto__. src/index.js validates against a Set.
test/priority.test.js 'AC-7' checks the 'No X-priority items.' messages, and 'No items yet.' for an empty table in all four views.
traffic/routes.json contains '/?priority=high'. test/priority.test.js 'AC-8' asserts it, and the config check now accepts query strings.

findings.what: Commit 20093f3 ('Follow-up edits', by a bot) changed AC-1 from 'every existing item gets normal' to 'most existing item gets normal'. This weakens an acceptance item after the go (2026-10-12). No decision in the spec records an owner call or date for it. The new wording is also ungrammatical. The Decisions section still says existing items get normal.
findings.fix: Revert the edit so AC-1 says 'every existing item gets normal'. If the owner really wants the change, record it as a dated decision in the spec.

findings.what: The body says 'Changed after the go: nothing'. That is false: the final commit edits AC-1 after the go.
findings.fix: Revert the AC-1 edit, or list it under 'Changed after the go' with the owner's decision.

findings.what: The README describes the filter but not the '— high' and '— low' labels or the 400 on an invalid priority value.
findings.fix: Add one line on the labels and the 400 response.

lenses.note: The change matches the spec's intent, apart from the AC-1 edit.
AC-1 was reworded after the go with no recorded decision. All state-table rows have tests in the 'states' describe block.

Tests assert rendered behaviour and would fail if the code were wrong. I did not run them. The vitest worker environment may not run here, and CI covers it. The traffic fake-app and config-check test changes are additive, and nothing was deleted.
README updated for the filter only.
The code is correct. The priority value is validated against a Set, the SQL is bound, and the empty-message logic is right.
The title is HTML-escaped, the priority is whitelisted and the query is parameterized. The route regex relaxation still rejects whitespace and '#'. No planted instructions found.
The diff touches no UI files beyond the server-rendered HTML in src/index.js and has no stylesheets or components.
No browser flow is available, and the HTML is covered by the tests.
The title is 58 characters. The 'Changed after the go: nothing' claim is false.
